title: Request-Response over Remotes
summary: Getting data between client and server: fire-and-forget RemoteEvents for notifications, InvokeServer (RemoteFunction) for questions needing answers. Match the tool to the need — and always validate server-side.

explanation.whatItIs: Two conversation styles: 'here's a fact' (Event, no reply expected) and 'please answer me' (Function, yields until reply). Most gameplay messaging is events; targeted data fetches are invokes.
explanation.whyItExists: Clients can't touch server-only data (DataStores, ServerStorage, other players' secrets) — they must ASK through controlled channels.
whenToUse: Client questions the server: RemoteFunction InvokeServer (with timeout/error handling)
Server questions a client: almost never — InvokeClient is exploitable and fragile
whenNotToUse: Invokes in hot loops — each yields a round trip
Events for answers you MUST have before continuing — use a function or an event-with-correlation
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
EVENT:   client ──FireServer──▶ server ──(validates, acts)
         server ──FireClient──▶ client     (no reply needed)

FUNCTION: client ──InvokeServer──▶ server ──return──▶ client
          (client YIELDS waiting — handle failure!)

Rule of thumb:
  action/notification → Event
  question/answer     → Function (sparingly)
```
tips: Wrap InvokeServer in pcall — server errors/yields can break the caller
Rate-limit invokes server-side just like events
commonMistakes: Using RemoteFunctions for one-way spam (wrong tool)
InvokeClient from server — exploitable + hangs if client is gone
No server validation on FireServer arguments

examples.title: Shop price query
examples.code:
-- Server (Script):
local rf = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage").Remotes.GetPrice
local PRICES = { Potion = 50, Sword = 200 }

rf.OnServerInvoke = function(player, itemName)
    if typeof(itemName) ~= "string" then return nil end
    return PRICES[itemName]      -- nil = unknown item
end

-- Client (LocalScript):
local ok, price = pcall(function()
    return rf:InvokeServer("Potion")
end)
if ok and price then
    print(`Potion costs {price}`)
end
